text: Capturing the WPA2 four-way handshake permits an offline dictionary attack against the passphrase.
explanation: True, which is why passphrase length matters enormously and why WPA3's SAE replaced the mechanism with one that is not offline-attackable. The KRACK vulnerability of 2017 attacked the handshake's state machine rather than its cryptography — protocols fail at their state machines at least as often as at their algorithms.
